newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATHLETICS-S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT BACKS CAPE TOWN 2004 BID.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-S.AFRICAN PARLIAMENT BACKS CAPE TOWN 2004 BID.

text.p: South Africa's national assembly on Tuesday threw its full weight behind Cape Town's bid for the 2004 Olympics after the city had been nominated for the short list of potential host cities.
Chief whip and African National Congress legislator Max Sisulu introduced a motion that said that the assembly hoped Cape Town would be the first African city to host the games.
Other cities that have qualified for the short list are Rome, Athens, Stockholm and Buenos Aires.
All minority parties backed Cape Town as well. They said they hoped everything would be done by government to ensure that Cape Town won the bid and showed that South Africa was "a winning nation".
